slots_and_copies.name: slot_0
slots_and_copies.selection_rule: Only copy present. No mirrored/backup slot in the 512-byte image: layout is header (0x00-0x17) + five 32B records (0x18-0xb7) + three 108B records (0xb8-0x1fb) + trailer (0x1fc-0x1ff). record108_1==record108_2 in sav-01 is template duplication, not slot redundancy; no generation/sequence counter found anywhere (header bytes identical in both snapshots, no incrementing field).

magic_signatures.ascii: S YENSID   RECCO (raw .sav order); DISNEY SOCCER   (logical RAM order after per-8-byte-block reversal)

checksums.name: unidentified - candidate stored u16 at logical 0x10 (0xc78f), no standard algorithm verified
checksums.formula_detail: No verified checksum. Exhaustive Python search (sum8, sum16 byte-sum, sum16/sum32 LE-word sums and complements, xor8/xor16, CRC16 Modbus/CCITT/XMODEM/Kermit, CRC32 and complement, Adler32, weighted sums) over all 8-byte-aligned start/end ranges in both raw .sav order and rev8 logical order on both samples produced no non-spurious match to stored 0xc78f/0x8fc7 at logical 0x10, nor to any plausible header/trailer stored value. Representative computed-vs-stored (rev8, sav-01): range 0x00-0x200 sum16=0x3a46 crc16modbus=0x7818 crc32=0x8cc4934d; range 0x18-0xb8 sum16=0x29bd crc16modbus=0xde91 crc32=0xddd9b236; all != 0xc78f. Integrity may rely on magic alone, on a custom/bitwise algorithm in the untraced writer gap (0x080fc46c-0x080fc5dc), or the u16 at 0x10 may not be a checksum at all. Confidence UNKNOWN; fuzzing must treat checksum repair as unknown.

io_driver_functions.notes: EEPROM read of one 8-byte block: param1=block address (&0xffff, bounds-checked vs *(u16*)(type+4)), address bits from type+8, sends (addr_bits+3)-bit serial command via FUN_080fc338 to 0x0d000000, then DMAs 0x44 halfwords back and reassembles 4 u16s MSB-first into RAM at param2+6,+4,+2,+0 (hence per-8-byte reversal between .sav and RAM). NO callers in callgraph.json and no func_0x080fc3b8 reference in decompiled.c - caller is indirect/untraced. This is the sole proven save-bus reader.

DMA3 driver: saves/restores interrupt/DMA regs via _DAT_080fc398.., writes src/dst to DMA3 regs (_DAT_080fc3a8/_DAT_080fc3ac), control = count&0xffff | 0x80000000 (enable), spins on DMA busy bit 0x8000. Used for both EEPROM serial TX (buffer->0x0d000000) and RX (0x0d000000->buffer) inside FUN_080fc3b8. Generic DMA, not save-specific.

Candidate EEPROM type/size select (SDK): param 4 and 0x40 select different type-table entries via _DAT_080fc1e0/_DAT_080fc1f4, else error 1. Static-only, no callers traced; supports EEPROM_V122 type dispatch but exact size mapping unresolved (DAT placeholders).
Candidate EEPROM type identify/set (SDK): if param1<=3 stores type byte and type-table pointer (*param2), else returns true. Static-only, no callers traced.

FALSE-POSITIVE seed from save_related_functions.c: gameplay/entity update (uses FUN_08045e48/FUN_08045e80/FUN_08045ec4 RNG-like helpers and FUN_08000110 jumptable stub). No EEPROM/DMA3/MMIO save I/O. Listed here only to close the seed; callers in save_related header: none in callgraph for this addr as save path.
FALSE-POSITIVE seed: unsigned modulo runtime helper (shifts/subtracts, calls func_0x080fc6ac on div-by-zero). No save I/O. Callers: none.

caller_chains.trigger_context: EEPROM 8-byte block read (serial command + DMA3 via 0x0d000000). Entry caller itself has no traced caller: callgraph.json callers=[] and no direct reference in decompiled.c, so the game-side save manager that passes the RAM destination (param2) and block address (param1) is indirect or in the untraced gap. How mapped: matched 0xd000000 literal in FUN_080fc3b8 + DMA3 register writes in FUN_080fc338 + rev8 magic reconstruction.
caller_chains.how_mapped: Code literal 0xd000000 (EEPROM window) in FUN_080fc3b8; DMA3 pattern in FUN_080fc338; callgraph edge 0x080fc3b8->0x080fc338 is the only save-bus edge in the corpus.

fields.name: magic_disney_soccer
fields.update_mechanism: Written once at save creation/format (writer not in traced corpus); read back and compared by unseen save manager (inferred). Raw .sav bytes are byte-reversed per 8-byte EEPROM block; logical RAM order is DISNEY SOCCER + 3 spaces.
fields.evidence: rev8(raw[0:16]) == b'DISNEY SOCCER   ' in both files; FUN_080fc3b8 (0x080fc3b8) reconstructs each 8-byte EEPROM block into RAM in exactly this reversed-u16 order (writes u16s to param2+6,+4,+2,+0). Note SOCCER (not Basketball) is literal in both samples - shared comm-009 engine heritage, not a transcription error. Raw offset 0x00, raw bytes 53 20 59 45 4e 53 49 44 20 20 20 52 45 43 43 4f

fields.name: record108_0
fields.update_mechanism: Whole-record flush by unseen writer in 8-byte blocks. sav-00: record108_1 only written up to ~0x150 and record108_2 still erased 0xff; sav-01: all written (mostly 0x00). Suggests sequential/lazy block writes across frames 1501-1525, not a second save slot.
fields.evidence: 108-byte record at logical 0xb8. Sparse single-bit bytes recur at identical internal offsets in all three records: +0x2a=0x10, +0x3c=0x01, +0x5c=0x01 (logical). record108_1 == record108_2 byte-for-byte in sav-01 (verified); record108_0 differs only at +0..+5 (00*6 vs fd 7e bf df ef 03) and +9 (0x01 vs 0x00).

fuzzing_targets.mutation: Raw .sav: flip first raw byte 0x53->0x54 (logical last magic byte). Reload from sav-01-pre.ss-equivalent state.
fuzzing_targets.predicted_effect: If magic is the only integrity gate, save is rejected/reinitialised (blank/default save, visual delta vs preserved save). If it loads, magic is not checked on this path.

fuzzing_targets.mutation: Logical 0x10: change 8f c7 -> 8e c7 (raw .sav offset 0x16-0x17 reversed in block: raw bytes at 0x10 block are 00 00 00 3f 3f 3f c7 8f, so edit raw 0x17).
fuzzing_targets.predicted_effect: If this u16 is a checksum, save rejected despite intact magic. If it loads unchanged, it is an ID/settings field, not integrity.
Watch for changed counts/limits/defaults in UI, or rejection if these are structural counts. No change suggests padding/settings.

fuzzing_targets.mutation: Logical record32_4 (0x98): revert its 6 divergent bytes to record32_0 template values (+0 0x46->0x32, +6 0xf0->0xa0, +12 0x21->0xe1, +13 0xa3->0xa1, +19 0x8a->0x85, +25 0x1e->0x0a), one byte at a time.
fuzzing_targets.predicted_effect: One in-game entity/stat should revert to default if record32_4 is the active entity; no visible change suggests it is an unused template slot.

fuzzing_targets.mutation: Logical record108_0 header 0xb8: 00*6 -> fd 7e bf df ef 03 (copy record108_1 header).
fuzzing_targets.predicted_effect: If dense header is a flag bitmask, many unlocks/progress bits should appear; if it is data, expect garbled progress. Tests the bitmask hypothesis.

fuzzing_targets.mutation: Logical 0xe2: 0x10 -> 0x00 and -> 0x11 (toggle sparse flag bits in record108_0 at +0x2a). Repeat at 0x14e/0x1ba equivalents.
fuzzing_targets.predicted_effect: Single progress/unlock flag should toggle in UI/RAM mirror; observe which menu/team state changes.

fuzzing_targets.mutation: Logical: overwrite record108_1 (0x124) with record108_0 (0xb8) bytes and vice versa.
fuzzing_targets.predicted_effect: If 108-records are profiles/slots, the swapped profile should become active; identical behaviour suggests template/backup copies.
If trailer is an end marker/final flag, save may be treated as incomplete and rewritten or rejected; no effect suggests a spare flag bit.

fuzzing_targets.mutation: Use sav-00 image (0x150-0x1ff still 0xff) vs sav-01 image as-is, reload each from paired states.
fuzzing_targets.predicted_effect: Counterfactual already in corpus: sav-00 must be accepted up to its written prefix (it was the live save at frame 1501), proving the loader does not require the 0x150-0x1ff region to be non-0xff - i.e. writes are lazy/sequential and no whole-image checksum over 0x00-0x200 with the stored u16 unchanged can be valid for both files unless it excludes the tail.

open_questions: Who calls FUN_080fc3b8? No direct caller in callgraph.json/decompiled.c; the save manager and the RAM mirror base (0x02xxxxxx/0x03xxxxxx - param2 destination) are unknown. DAT_* placeholders in the 0x080fc cluster are unresolved, so RAM addresses cannot be named honestly.

Where is the EEPROM write driver? Address gap 0x080fc46c-0x080fc5dc (0x224 bytes after FUN_080fc3b8) is not in the 591 traced functions and is the natural location for the SDK write/verify routine; the serializer and any checksum routine likely live there or in the same untraced caller.
Is the u16 at logical 0x10 (0xc78f) a checksum, an ID, or data? No standard algorithm reproduced it; a custom algorithm cannot be ruled out.

What do the five 32-byte records and three 108-byte records mean semantically (teams/players/profiles/progress)? Only template-vs-divergent structure is proven; no code in the corpus mutates them by name.
Why does the magic say DISNEY SOCCER in a Basketball title? Literal in both .sav files after rev8 reconstruction; presumed shared comm-009 engine save code, unproven beyond the bytes.

EEPROM geometry: file is 512 bytes (64 x 8-byte blocks, EEPROM 4Kbit from PACKET). FUN_080fc3b8 takes address-bit count from type struct (+8) and block count from +4; neither value is resolved in decompiled.c, so 6-bit block addressing is inferred from media size, not read from code.
Generation/selection: no sequence counter or backup slot found; if the game keeps redundancy, it is outside the 512-byte EEPROM image.
